New-Hire Onboarding
Onboarding
Your first week at Quiz Lab — how it's built, how it ships, and how work flows through Studio AI.
#1f6feb
onb-content-1
In the Quiz Lab repo, where do the quiz pack files live?
In static/quizzes/, one file per quiz
In app/src/lib/data/packs/, one JSON file per pack
In a Postgres table managed by a content API
Inside app/src/routes/, next to the page components

Each pack is a single JSON file in app/src/lib/data/packs/, which the loader (packs.ts) reads directly. The static/quizzes/ path is from the deprecated v0 format and is no longer used. (Architecture Overview; ARCHITECTURE.md)
onb-content-2
How does a merged content change actually reach the live Quiz Lab site?
It's pushed to a Vercel deployment with worldwide edge caching
An admin uploads the new pack through a dashboard
A nightly cron job syncs the packs into a database
Merging to main triggers a GitHub Actions build that publishes the static site to GitHub Pages

The whole deploy pipeline is: merge to main → GitHub Actions builds the static site → it's published to GitHub Pages. There is no Vercel deployment and no manual upload step. (Architecture Overview; ONBOARDING.md §5)
onb-content-3
What backend database does Quiz Lab use to store packs in v1?
Postgres
DynamoDB
None — it's a fully prerendered static site and all content ships in the build
A SQLite file committed to the repo

Quiz Lab is intentionally backend-less in v1: a static SvelteKit app (adapter-static + prerender) served from GitHub Pages, with all content shipped in the build. Marketing copy that mentions Postgres is aspirational, not the live architecture. (ARCHITECTURE.md; Architecture Overview)
onb-content-4
What is the entire process for adding a new pack to Quiz Lab?
Run a database migration, then redeploy the API
Drop a new JSON file into the packs directory and open a PR — no backend changes
Add a row through the analytics dashboard
Edit static/quizzes/ and call the content API to reindex
Adding a pack is one file change plus one PR: drop a JSON file in app/src/lib/data/packs/ and open a PR. There's no backend and no migration. (README 'Adding a new pack'; Architecture Overview)
onb-dev-1
How do you run Quiz Lab locally, and what URL does the dev server use?
npm run dev → http://localhost:5173
npm run dev → http://localhost:3000
npm start → http://localhost:8080
vercel dev → http://localhost:5173
From the app/ directory you run npm install then npm run dev, which serves on http://localhost:5173. (README 'Getting started'; Architecture Overview 'Local development')
onb-dev-2
What must pass before a Quiz Lab PR can merge?
A manual QA sign-off in the dashboard
A passing database migration
npm run build — a broken build blocks the GitHub Pages deploy
Nothing automated; merges are unrestricted
npm run build (in app/) must pass before a PR merges, because a broken build would block the Pages deploy. (Architecture Overview 'Local development'; task spec)
onb-dev-3
Which stack is Quiz Lab actually built on?
Next.js deployed on Vercel
React Native with Expo
SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 (runes mode), built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-static
A plain static HTML site with no build step

Quiz Lab is SvelteKit 2 with Svelte 5 in runes mode, bundled by Vite and output by @sveltejs/adapter-static for GitHub Pages. React Native is only an unscheduled roadmap idea, and there is no Next.js/Vercel. (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Tech Stack')
onb-schema-1
In the current pack schema, how many choices must each question have?
Exactly 4
Any number, usually 3
Between 2 and 6
At least 4
A question's choices is a 4-tuple — exactly 4 options. The 'any length, often 3' rule belongs to the deprecated v0 format. (Pack Authoring Guide; packs.ts type [string, string, string, string])
onb-schema-2
How is the correct answer recorded on a question?
As a string in a 'correct' field
As correctIndex, an integer from 0 to 3 pointing into the choices array
As a boolean flag on each choice
In a separate answer-key file

The correct answer is correctIndex, an integer 0–3 indexing into choices. Storing the answer as a 'correct' string is the old v0 shape and is invalid now. (Pack Authoring Guide; ARCHITECTURE.md 'Data Model')
onb-schema-3
Besides id, prompt, and choices, which fields does every question require?
Only a 'correct' string; difficulty and explanation are optional
correctIndex, difficulty (1–3), and explanation
tags and a coverEmoji
A timestamp and an author handle

Every question needs correctIndex (0–3), difficulty (1–3, where 1 = easy and 3 = hard), and an explanation shown after answering. The v0 format had no difficulty or explanation. (Pack Authoring Guide; ARCHITECTURE.md 'Data Model')
onb-studio-1
In the Studio AI MCP workflow, which tool do you use to start work on a task?
work_on_next_task — it marks the task inProgress and assigns it to the agent
submit_for_review
create_task
load_product_context
work_on_next_task picks up a task (a specific number, or the oldest backlog item), moves it to inProgress, and binds it to the agent. (ONBOARDING.md §10; Studio AI SDLC & MCP)
onb-studio-2
How does a task move into the 'review' state?
Any inProgress task is reviewed automatically every night
By deploying it to production
A reviewer manually drags it there after the PR merges
By submitting work with a PR (via submit_for_review); merging the PR then auto-transitions it to done

Submitting work with a PR moves the task to review and assigns reviewers; without a PR it goes straight to done. When the PR is merged, the task auto-transitions to done. (ONBOARDING.md §7 & §9; Studio AI SDLC & MCP)
onb-studio-3
How many agents or people can hold a given task in 'inProgress' at the same time?
Unlimited — tasks are collaborative by default
Exactly one; another agent must wait until it's released or moved on
Up to one per branch
Two: an author and a reviewer
Only one agent or person can have a task inProgress at a time; a second pick-up attempt fails until the current owner releases it. (ONBOARDING.md §7 'Task')
